title: Disconnected Domain Model Aggregates Querying Repositories
pattern: An Aggregate Root receiving and executing queries on database repositories inside its own business logic methods.
why_bad: It introduces lazy-loading exceptions, database connection details, and heavy I/O operations deep inside the aggregate boundary. This makes unit testing highly painful due to complex mocking requirements.
detection: Methods defined on core business entities that accept arguments typed as repositories or data access traits.
counterexample: Pure domain services or application services designed specifically to coordinate logic across aggregates.
source: *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* by Vaughn Vernon (Chapter 10, p. 362-363; "Disconnected Domain Model").
